title: Framed mapping complexes and derived diagram adjunctions in simplicial categories
statement:
Use the ordinary Bergner model category of small simplicial categories and the framed homotopy function complexes $\operatorname{Map}^h(-,-)$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping], not a simplicial model structure on that category. Thus a cosimplicial resolution $U^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}C$ is Reedy cofibrant, with every augmentation a weak equivalence and $U^0\to C$ a cofibrant replacement; for fibrant $T$, its mapping complex has $n$-simplices $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(U^n,T)$. Use Reedy objects as in [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] and injective derived limits as in [lem-coef-combinatorial-injective-diagram-model]. Let $J$ be a small ordinary category, and suppose the diagram categories in use have projective model structures with objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations. Write $\operatorname{hocolim}_J D=\operatorname{colim}_J QD$ for projective cofibrant replacement, and $\operatorname{holim}_J D=\operatorname{lim}_J RD$ for injective fibrant replacement. The same conventions in Kan-model simplicial sets define homotopy limits of spaces. Then for every $D:J\to\mathrm{sCat}$, every $C$ and every $T$, there are natural weak equivalences
$$\operatorname{Map}^h(\operatorname{hocolim}_J D,T)\simeq\operatorname{holim}_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}^h(D(j),T),\qquad
\operatorname{Map}^h(C,\operatorname{holim}_J D)\simeq\operatorname{holim}_{j\in J}\operatorname{Map}^h(C,D(j)).$$
They carry the maps induced by each cocone or cone to the corresponding mapping-complex comparisons. They are compatible, by natural weak-equivalence zigzags, with maps between augmented cosimplicial resolutions of entire diagrams. In particular for a Reedy cofibrant homotopically constant $V^\bullet$ in the projective model category $\mathrm{sCat}^{J}$ resolving $D$, and fibrant $T$, the strict diagram $j\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(V^\bullet(j),T)$ may be used on the right of the first formula. No condition that $J$ be nonempty is imposed.

source.place: Hirschhorn, Model Categories and Their Localizations, Theorem 19.4.4(1),(2), printed p.415 (PDF p.429); natural frame comparison is Theorem 19.4.3 and Corollaries 19.3.6--19.3.7, printed pp.413--415. Read from rendered pages 2026-10-17; PDF retained in item work/hirschhornloc.pdf. Projective/injective derived-functor conventions are assumed explicitly, not a claim of simplicial enrichment on sCat. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: First record the elementary Quillen checks needed for the chosen replacements. The adjunction $\operatorname{colim}_J\dashv\operatorname{const}$ is left Quillen for the projective structure: the constant functor takes a (trivial) fibration to an objectwise (trivial) fibration. Evaluation at $j$ is also left Quillen for that structure. Its right adjoint sends $Z$ to the diagram $k\mapsto\prod_{J(k,j)}Z$; its value on a (trivial) fibration is a product of (trivial) fibrations, with fillers chosen in each factor. Both left adjoints consequently preserve weak equivalences between cofibrant objects. For completeness this last assertion follows from [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations]: for a weak equivalence $f=pi$ with $ps=1$ and $i,s$ cofibrations, two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations; applying the left adjoint and using $Lp\,Ls=1$ proves that $Lp$ and then $Lf$ are weak equivalences. This argument applies also to the Reedy model categories of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] whenever the adjunction is lifted there.

source.place: Theorem 19.4.4, printed p.415; agent calculation with projective/injective replacements

proof.text: Choose a Reedy cofibrant homotopically constant resolution $V^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}D$ in the projective model category of $J$-diagrams, and replace $T$ by a fibrant $RT$. Such a resolution exists by functorial Reedy factorization, with its degree-zero cofibrant replacement fixed, using [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. The degree-zero diagram $V^0$ is projectively cofibrant. Evaluation, by Step 1, preserves latching colimits and the latching cofibrations; thus every $V^\bullet(j)$ is a cosimplicial resolution of $D(j)$. Likewise $A^\bullet=\operatorname{colim}_J V^\bullet$ is Reedy cofibrant. Each $V^n\to V^0$ is a weak equivalence between projectively cofibrant diagrams, so Step 1 implies that $A^n\to A^0$ is a weak equivalence. Therefore $A^\bullet$ is a frame on $A^0=\operatorname{colim}_J V^0$, a permitted representative of $\operatorname{hocolim}_J D$. By [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping] the complexes $\operatorname{Hom}(A^\bullet,RT)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(V^\bullet(j),RT)$ compute respectively the desired mapping spaces from this homotopy colimit and from $D(j)$.

source.place: Theorem 19.4.4, printed p.415; agent calculation with projective/injective replacements

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-projective-frame-weighted-coend] with $\mathcal M=\mathrm{sCat}$ to this whole-diagram resolution. Its right adjoint sends the fibrant object $RT$ to an injectively fibrant diagram $F:J^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{sSet}$, where $F(j)=\operatorname{Hom}(V^\bullet(j),RT)$: the right adjoint preserves fibrations and the terminal object by the adjunction lifting test. The source of that Quillen adjunction is the injective space-diagram model, so this conclusion is stronger than merely saying that each $F(j)$ is Kan. The Kan model structure is combinatorial: $\mathrm{sSet}$ is a presheaf category, hence locally presentable, and by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] its cofibrations and trivial cofibrations are generated by the sets of boundary and horn inclusions; so the injective structure on $\mathrm{sSet}^{J^{\mathrm{op}}}$ exists. By [lem-coef-combinatorial-injective-diagram-model], $\lim_{J^{\mathrm{op}}}F$ consequently computes $\operatorname{holim}_{J^{\mathrm{op}}}F$.

source.place: Theorem 19.4.4, printed p.415; agent calculation with projective/injective replacements

proof.text:
In every simplicial degree the ordinary colimit universal property gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(\operatorname{colim}_J V^n,RT)=\lim_{j\in J^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(V^n(j),RT).$$
The bijection sends a map to its restrictions along the colimit legs and its inverse glues a compatible family. Precomposition by each cosimplicial operator commutes with restricting, so these bijections form an isomorphism of simplicial sets $\operatorname{Hom}(A^\bullet,RT)\cong\lim F$. Together with Steps 2–3 this is the first equivalence. In particular, if the given $T$ is fibrant, it permits exactly the strict diagram built from the given whole-diagram resolution $V^\bullet$, namely $j\mapsto\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{sCat}}(V^\bullet(j),T)$.

source.place: Theorem 19.4.4, printed p.415; agent calculation with projective/injective replacements

proof.text: For the second formula choose a cosimplicial frame $U^\bullet$ on a cofibrant replacement $QC\to C$, and an injective fibrant replacement $D\to RD$. Define $L_UK=\int^{[n]}U^n\cdot K_n$ and $R_UZ=\operatorname{Hom}(U^\bullet,Z)$; the coend relations give $L_U\dashv R_U$. The coend universal property gives $L_U\Delta^n=U^n$ and $L_U\partial\Delta^n=L_nU^\bullet$. Hence the boundary maps are cofibrations by Reedy cofibrancy, and the collapses $L_U\Delta^n\to L_U\Delta^0$ are weak equivalences by homotopical constancy. The boundary-collapse theorem [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] implies that $L_U$ is left Quillen and $R_U$ is right Quillen. This uses the ordinary model structure only, without a simplicial enrichment on $\mathrm{sCat}$.

source.place: Theorem 19.4.4, printed p.415; agent calculation with projective/injective replacements

proof.text:
The Bergner structure is combinatorial: $\mathrm{sCat}$ is locally presentable by [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and the model structure of [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping] has its two weak factorization systems generated by the sets $I,J$ there; so [lem-coef-combinatorial-injective-diagram-model] applies to $\mathrm{sCat}^J$ and $RD$ exists. Apply the adjunction $L_U\dashv R_U$ objectwise to $J$-diagrams. The left adjoint preserves injective cofibrations and injective trivial cofibrations, because these are objectwise and $L_U$ is left Quillen. The right adjoint therefore sends the injectively fibrant $RD$ to an injectively fibrant space diagram $G(j)=\operatorname{Hom}(U^\bullet,RD(j))$. Also $RD(j)$ and $\lim_J RD$ are fibrant by [lem-coef-combinatorial-injective-diagram-model]. The ordinary limit universal property, in every degree, gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(U^\bullet,\lim_J RD)\cong\lim_J\operatorname{Hom}(U^\bullet,RD(-))=\lim_JG.$$
By [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping] the left side computes $\operatorname{Map}^h(C,\operatorname{holim}_J D)$ and $G(j)$ computes $\operatorname{Map}^h(C,D(j))$. The injective fibrancy of $G$ makes its strict limit a representative of its homotopy limit. This proves the second formula.

source.place: Theorem 19.4.4, printed p.415; agent calculation with projective/injective replacements

proof.text: The comparisons have the claimed cone and cocone maps, not just equivalent endpoints. Given a cocone $D\to\operatorname{const}B$, factor the induced map $A^\bullet=\operatorname{colim}_JV^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}B$ in the Reedy model category of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure] as a Reedy cofibration $A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ followed by a Reedy trivial fibration $B^\bullet\to\operatorname{const}B$. Then $B^\bullet$ is Reedy cofibrant with objectwise weak-equivalence augmentation, so it is a frame on the cofibrant replacement $B^0\to B$ and computes $\operatorname{Map}^h(B,T)$ by [lem-coef-simplicial-derived-pushout-mapping]. Precomposition with $A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$, followed by the isomorphism of Step 4, sends a map $B^n\to RT$ to the family of composites $V^n(j)\to A^n\to B^n\to RT$; over the augmentations these lie over the cocone legs $D(j)\to B$, so this is the map induced by the cocone. Dually, for a cone $B\to D(j)$, factor the induced $B\to\lim_JRD$ as a trivial cofibration $B\to RB$ followed by a fibration $RB\to\lim_JRD$; a map $U^n\to RB$ is sent to its composites $U^n\to RB\to\lim_JRD\to RD(j)$, which is the limit comparison of Step 6 followed by the map induced by the cone. These descriptions commute with every simplex operator, diagram arrow, and map of cones or cocones, since composition is associative. Choosing these factorizations functorially makes the comparisons natural before passing to weak-equivalence zigzags.

source.place: Theorem 19.4.4, printed p.415; agent calculation with projective/injective replacements

proof.text: Here is an explicit resolution-comparison argument, so compatibility does not depend on an unspecified identification of frame choices. In any of the Reedy model categories in use, a trivial cofibration $a:A^\bullet\to B^\bullet$ has trivial-cofibration relative latching maps, by [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. A boundary lifting problem for $\operatorname{Hom}(B^\bullet,T)\to\operatorname{Hom}(A^\bullet,T)$ is exactly a square from $A^n\amalg_{L_nA}L_nB\to B^n$ against $T\to *$. If $T$ is fibrant it has a filler. The boundary test of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper] therefore makes this map a trivial Kan fibration. For a weak equivalence $a$ between Reedy cofibrant resolutions, apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] in the Reedy model category to write $a=pi$, $ps=1$ with $i,s$ cofibrations. Two-out-of-three makes $i,s$ trivial cofibrations. The maps induced contravariantly by $i,s$ are weak equivalences by the boundary argument; $ps=1$ then makes the maps induced by $p$ and $a$ weak equivalences. This applies in particular at every $j$ to maps of whole-diagram resolutions, since evaluation preserves the required Reedy cofibrancy and weak equivalences by Steps 1–2.

source.place: Agent relative-latching boundary lifting and split-factorization proof of frame comparison, underlying Hirschhorn Corollaries 19.3.6–19.3.7.

proof.text: For a map of augmented whole-diagram resolutions $V^\bullet\to W^\bullet$, its components are weak equivalences by two-out-of-three with the augmentations. Step 8 consequently gives an objectwise weak equivalence of the corresponding strict $J^{\mathrm{op}}$-diagrams of mapping complexes. Both diagrams are injectively fibrant by [lem-coef-projective-frame-weighted-coend]. The limit is right Quillen by [lem-coef-combinatorial-injective-diagram-model]; the dual split-factorization argument from [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] makes it preserve weak equivalences between fibrant objects. Thus taking their strict limits gives the required natural weak-equivalence comparison, and the strict restriction identities of Step 7 show that it commutes with cocone maps. Apply Step 8 also to maps between choices of $U^\bullet$ in Step 6. The diagrams $R_U^J(RD)$ are injectively fibrant by Step 6, so the same limit argument proves the second comparison and its cone compatibility. Functorial replacements and refinements in the Reedy model categories yield the corresponding natural zigzags whenever a comparison is expressed as a zigzag rather than a single map.

source.place: Theorem 19.4.4, printed p.415; agent calculation with projective/injective replacements

proof.text: When $J=\varnothing$, $\operatorname{hocolim}_J D$ is the initial simplicial category $\varnothing$ and $\operatorname{holim}_J D$ is the terminal simplicial category. The constant cosimplicial object at $\varnothing$ is a cofibrant frame and has a unique map into every target in every degree. The terminal object is fibrant and receives a unique map from every frame in every degree. Thus both left sides are the one-point simplicial set, as are both empty homotopy limits of spaces. The displayed isomorphisms and all cone/cocone comparisons give these unique maps, so the proof includes the empty case.
